user.title: Add an AI pool
user.description: A pool publishes one entity that routes calls across several providers.

data_description.name: Shown on the pool entity and on its diagnostic sensors.
data_description.pool_type: Which domain the pool publishes in. This cannot be changed afterwards, because it decides which platform is loaded.

members.title: Members and policy
members.description: Members are tried in the order the strategy decides. A failing member is skipped and the next one is tried.

data.timeout_seconds: Give up on a member after

data_description.members: Entities of this pool's domain, in preference order. Pool entities are excluded so a pool cannot contain itself.
data_description.strategy: How the next member is chosen when several are healthy. Round robin spreads daily quotas; priority is pure failover.
data_description.cooldown_seconds: How long a member sits out after a capacity refusal. Consecutive refusals double this, up to an hour.
data_description.max_attempts: How many members to try for one request before giving up.
data_description.timeout_seconds: How long to wait for one member before abandoning it and trying the next. 0 waits forever.
data_description.stt_buffer_limit: How much of a recording to keep so a second member can hear the same audio. A recording larger than this is clipped and gets one attempt with no failover. The default is 8 MB.

limits.title: Allowances
limits.description: For each member of {members}, three numbers in order: requests per day (req/day), requests per minute (req/min), then the routing weight. Use 0 where the limit is unknown. Providers do not report remaining quota, so these numbers only steer the rotation — a real refusal is always detected from the error. Google publishes no fixed figures and does not guarantee them: read your own in AI Studio, and note they apply per project rather than per API key.

abort.already_configured: A pool of that type already fronts exactly these members. Two pools over the same members each keep their own counters and each believe they hold the whole allowance.

init.description: The pool type cannot be changed after creation.

error.duplicate_members: Another pool already fronts exactly these members, and two pools over the same members would each spend the allowance as if they were alone.

duplicate_model.title: Members of {pool} share a model on the same account
duplicate_model.description: Several members of {pool} use the same model on the same API key: {models}. Two accounts on one model split daily quotas; two entities of one account do not. Point them at different models, or remove the duplicate.

reset_member.name: Reset a member
reset_member.description: Clear the cooldown, the spent-allowance mark and the permanent disable held against a pool member, so it is tried again immediately.

pool.name: Pool
pool.description: Which pool the member belongs to.

member.name: Member
member.description: The member entity to reset. Leave empty to reset every member of the pool.

clear_counters.name: Also clear today's counters
clear_counters.description: Lift an allowance the pool counted as spent, by forgetting how much the member has done today. Costs that member's metrics for the day, and is the only way to make it eligible again before midnight.

pool_not_found.message: No AI Pool config entry with id {pool}.

pool_not_loaded.message: The pool {pool} is not loaded, so it has nothing to reset.
